paper.title: Almost Optimal Channel Access in Multi-Hop Networks With Unknown Channel Variables

settings.name_in_paper: Linearly combinatorial MAB for multi-hop channel access (MWIS on extended conflict graph with unknown weights)
unmapped: feasible actions are independent sets of an extended conflict graph (unit-disk based) over K = N*M base arms (node-channel pairs)
distributed implementation over network nodes with communication constraints
regret measured against 1/beta fraction of optimum (beta-regret), with practical throughput factor theta for time spent on decisions
settings.definition_quote: our problem becomes a NP-hard combinatorial multi-armed bandits problem that selects at most $N$ arms (i.e., vertexes in $H$) out of $K=N M$ ones to minimize the regret $\mathfrak{R}$, such that these arms are independent from each other in $H$.

algorithms.name: Distributed channel access with learning policy of Zhou & Li and distributed robust PTAS (Algorithms 1-3)

bound.expression_latex: \frac{1}{\alpha} N K + \left( \theta \sqrt{e K} + \frac{16}{e\alpha}( 1+N)N^3 \right) n^{\frac{2}{3}} + \frac{1}{\alpha} \left( 1+ \frac{4 \sqrt{K} N^2}{e (\theta\alpha)^2} \right)N^2 K n^{\frac{5}{6}}

symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes (secondary users) in the network; max number of base arms per strategy
symbols.theta: fraction of round time spent on data transmission, t_d/t_a
symbols.alpha_apx: approximation ratio alpha of the distributed strategy-decision algorithm (practical regret uses theta*alpha)

conditions: channel data rates i.i.d. with means in [0,1]
tuning: index uses exploration bonus sqrt(max(ln(t^{2/3}/(K m)),0)/m)

source.quote: The practical regret of Algorithm 2 satisfies \sup \theta \mathfrak{R}_{\theta\alpha}(n) \leq \frac{1}{\alpha} N K + \left( \theta \sqrt{e K} + \frac{16}{e\alpha}( 1+N)N^3 \right) n^{\frac{2}{3}} + \frac{1}{\alpha} \left( 1+ \frac{4 \sqrt{K} N^2}{e (\theta\alpha)^2} \right)N^2 K n^{\frac{5}{6}}.

results.notes: Practical (theta-scaled) beta-regret with beta = theta*alpha; derived by applying Theorem 1 of Zhou & Li (cited). Regret is defined via expected play counts relative to R_1/beta. Approximation alpha from Theorem 4 holds only with constant probability in random networks; this caveat is not stated in the theorem. Theorems 2-4 are approximation-ratio results, not regret bounds, and were not extracted.

cited_results.cited_title: Multi-armed bandits with combinatorial strategies under stochastic bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic combinatorial semi-bandit with linear rewards in [0,1], K base arms, strategies of at most N arms, beta-approximation oracle; beta-regret
